chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Katib reported to me from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Za'farani, who reported from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, who reported from Abu Amr Hafs ibn Umar al-Farra, who reported from Zaid ibn al-Hasan al-Anmati, from Ma'ruf ibn Kharrabuz, who said: I heard Abu Ubaidullah, the client of al-Abbas, reporting to Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon them both), saying: I heard Abu Sa'id al-Khudri say:

The last sermon addressed to us by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was the one delivered during the illness in which he died. He came out leaning upon Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) and his freed maid Maymunah. He sat on the pulpit and said: 'O people, I am leaving among you the two weighty things,' and fell silent.

A man stood up and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what are these two weighty things?' He became upset until his face turned red, then he calmed down and said: 'I only mentioned them intending to inform you about them, but I was out of breath and could not continue. It is a rope, one end of which is in the hand of Allah and the other end is in your hands - you will deal with it in such and such a way. Be it known, it is the Quran, and the lesser weighty thing is my Ahlul Bayt.'

Then he said: 'By God, I am saying this to you while the unborn progeny in the loins of the polytheists give me more hope than many of you.' Then he said: 'By Allah, no servant loves them except that Allah will grant him a light on the Day of Resurrection until he arrives near me at the Pool, and no servant hates them except that Allah will be veiled from him on the Day of Resurrection.'
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Abu Ubaidullah brings to us that which he knows.'

key_terms.أهل بيتي: My Ahlul Bayt - the Prophet's household, specifically his family through Ali and Fatimah
key_terms.الثقلين: The Two Weighty Things (al-Thaqalayn) - referring to the Quran and the Ahlul Bayt, the Prophet's household
key_terms.الحوض: The Pool (al-Hawdh) - a basin in the afterlife from which the Prophet will give water to his followers

ai.seo_question: What is the Hadith al-Thaqalayn and what did the Prophet say in his last sermon about the Quran and Ahlul Bayt?
ai.summary: This hadith records the Prophet Muhammad's (SAWW) last sermon, delivered during his final illness, in which he explicitly designated the Quran and his Ahlul Bayt as the Two Weighty Things (al-Thaqalayn) left behind for the Muslim community. The sermon was addressed to the companions in Medina, and the Prophet's visible frustration at being interrupted reveals the gravity of this bequest. He warned that unborn children of polytheists gave him more hope than many of his current followers, and pronounced that loving the Ahlul Bayt leads to divine light on Judgment Day while hating them results in being veiled from God.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 3. He said: Abul Hasan ‘Ali ibn Muhammad al-Katib reported to me from al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali al-Za’farani, who reported from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, who reported from Abu Amru Hafs ibn Umar al-Farra, who reported from Zaid ibn al-Hasan al-Anmati, from Ma’roof ibn Kharrabuz, who said: I heard Abu Ubaidullah, the client of al-Abbas reporting to Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn ‘Ali, peace be upon him, saying: I heard Abu Saeed al-Khudari say:

The last sermon addressed by the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, was the one addressed to us during the illness in which he died. He came out leaning upon ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib peace be upon him, and his maid Maymoonah. He sat on the pulpit and said: "O people! I am leaving behind among you two weighty things." Then he remained silent.

A man stood up and said: "O messenger of Allah! What are these two weighty things?" The Prophet was upset till his face turned red and then it subsided. He said: "I did not mention them except with an intention to inform you, but you were in a haste, so I could not. It is a medium whose one end is with Allah, and the other end is in your hands, with whom you will do such a such thing. Be it known; they are the Qur’an and the smaller weighty thing, my Ahlul Bayt."

Then he said: "By Allah, I am saying this to you while I pin more hope on the unborn progeny of the infidels than upon most of you." And then he said: "By Allah, whoever loves them, Allah will bless them with a light on the Day of Judgement, till they arrive near me at the Pool. And whoever hates them, Allah will keep them away from Him on the Day of Judgement."
Abu Ja’far said: "Surely, Abu Ubaidullah has brought to us that of which he is aware."
